newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Natgas resources estimated at 1,039 tcf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Natgas resources estimated at 1,039 tcf.

text.p: The total U.S. natural gas resource base, including proven, probable and possible reserves, were estimated at 1,039 trillion cubic feet, the Potential Gas Committee said Wednesday.
The latest estimate was six percent higher than the previous estimate made in 1994 by the committee, which includes industry, government and academic officials.
The committee estimated total traditional natural gas resources at 741 tcf in 1996, up from 723 tcf in 1994.
The traditional resources included probable reserves in existing fields, possible reserves in new fields and speculative reserves in fields yet to be discovered.
The committee also estimated that coalbed methane resources could amount to 132 tcf, down from 134 tcf two years ago.
The estimate of total U.S. resources included proved natural gas reserves of 165 tcf, up from 162 tcf, according to Energy Department estimates.

The increases from estimates made two years ago were largely due to transfers of natural gas resources into proved reserves and analysis of new data in the North Central, Gulf Coast, and Rocky Mountain areas, the committee said.

The committee's estimates for 1996 were slightly lower than estimates made by the U.S. Geological Survey and Minerals Management Service, and the National Petroleum Council, which both saw U.S. potential natural gas resources closer to 1,200 tcf.
The Gas Resource Institute, another industry-funded group, has pegged U.S. gas resources at more than 1,900 tcf.
